answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with graduated trust earned through verified useful work. A new agent starts in a sandbox with tiny trade caps, like an opal kept behind glass: seen but not spent freely. Each completed job, checked by peers, earns trust credits that slowly raise its limits, so a haven for honest newcomers still exists while a flood of fresh fakes stays penned in. The anchor is time itself — building a thousand trusted identities takes weeks of real, paid-for work per identity, which costs a Sybil farm more than it can ever extract.
